newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault works council disappointed on Vilvoorde.
newsitem.headline: Renault works council disappointed on Vilvoorde.

text.p: Carmaker Renault SA's European works council said on Wednesday it was disappointed with what it called a "face-saving" decision to appoint an independent expert to study the proposed Vilvoorde plant closure.
"Its (the council's) initial response is that this mission looks like an escape that allows everyone to save face, Renault's management and the French government," it said in a statement.
"The Vilvoorde workers were expecting another decision after the commitments made during the election campaign."
Renault said on Tuesday that its board had commissioned an independent study to explore alternatives to the proposed closure.
The decision came less than two weeks after the election of a Socialist-led government, whose leader Lionel Jospin pledged to push 46 percent state-owned Renault to explore all alternatives.

Renault said that, if the study due before the end of the month showed the closure was necessary, it would implement a plan covering social measures for the 2,900 workers and work to establish "a significant industrial activity on the site."
The works council said the lack of precision on the alternative for the Belgian plant raised concerns that it might be an empty promise.
The National Assembly's Communist legislators will ask for a commission to study the French auto industry, legislator Georges Hage said on Wednesday.
In addition to the plant closure, Renault plans nearly 2,800 job cuts in France. Automobiles Peugeot, the biggest carmaking arm of PSA Peugeot Citroen, said last week that it planned 2,816 job cuts.

The CFTC union said in a statement that it estimated the number of job cuts in the French auto and auto parts industries at 10,000 this year. The French car industry employs between 700,000 and 800,000 people directly and indirectly.
